hints: Look closely at the structure of ethylene glycol, it has two -OH groups, so think about what type of intermolecular force it can make.
Remember ice is held together by a regular lattice of hydrogen bonds, so ask yourself what happens when a molecule that can also hydrogen bond is added.
Think about the rule that like dissolves like, and decide if a small molecule with two -OH groups will mix well with water.
walkthrough:
**Spot the hydrogen bonding groups**

Think of ethylene glycol as a small organic molecule with two alcohol groups. Each -OH can both donate and accept hydrogen bonds.

Structure to remember:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Explain how ice melts**

Ice is a giant open lattice held by extensive hydrogen bonds between water molecules. When ethylene glycol is added, it forms new hydrogen bonds to water and gets in the way of the regular ice lattice.

This disruption lowers the freezing point, so ice melts even below $0^{\circ}\text{C}$. This makes statement 1 correct.

**Check glycol to glycol bonding**

Because each molecule has O-H bonds attached to highly electronegative oxygen, one ethylene glycol molecule can hydrogen bond to another one. The H of one -OH is attracted to the lone pair on the O of another -OH. This makes statement 2 correct.

**Check solubility in water**

Water is a hydrogen-bonded polar solvent. Ethylene glycol is also small, polar and a strong hydrogen bonder, so it mixes and dissolves very well in the water formed from melting ice. This makes statement 3 correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the combination that includes all three statements is the right choice.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. Ethylene glycol disrupts ice hydrogen bonding, it hydrogen bonds to itself, and it dissolves in water because it can hydrogen bond to water.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only statements 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out statement 3. Students choose this if they think organic molecules do not dissolve in water, forgetting that small molecules with two -OH groups are very soluble.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only statements 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1. Students choose this if they do not link freezing point depression to disruption of the hydrogen bonded lattice in ice.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only statement 1. It wrongly leaves out statements 2 and 3. Students choose this if they think hydrogen bonding only happens with water, forgetting that any molecule with N-H, O-H or F-H can hydrogen bond to itself.
